tulā.cp: fem. a balance; scales; a rafter.
tulā.p: [Tala=tula+a+ā] (thī) CL=7 [Tulati saṅghāṭesu patiṭṭhātīti tulā, talapatiṭṭhāyaṃ, assuttaṃ. Pakkhānaṃ vā samavāhitabhāvakaraṇato tulayati mināti etāyāti tulā, tula ummāne. Kaṅkhā, yo, mahāṭī, 3. 386. Dhāna, ṭī. 223.(-479, 480-1).]  (1) a cross beam (which is a wooden plank that is placed horizontally position on top of the pillar of a house). (2) A beam supporting the floor joints (that is a wooden plank that is as well attached to the pillar of a house, as well passed through in the pillar of a house). (3) Libra (the seventh sign of the zodiac in the twelve zodiacs), Thadingyut month (the seventh month of the year, containing 29 days). (4) 100 Pala. (5) A Weight scale (or) A balance. (B) See also its meaning. (6) A basket that measures or weighs something, A Scale pan. It cites as an example, It is as a weigh the pros and cons. (7) As it is similar, Same. See also (5). (8) A holder attached to the fulcrum of a pair of scales. (9) An arm which is to draw water. (10) Things which are for weight. (11) It is bent. See - Tulākoṭi. (12) Center pin used in conjunction with pulley rope. See - Tulāruḷha. (13) The amount of weight. (14) It is similar. See also - Atula-(1). (15) (Kamma) which can be distinguished, (A) Kāmāvacarakaṃma. (B) Kāmāvacara Kamma, rūpāvacara kaṃma. (C) Kāma, Rūpa, Arūpa that has a little benefit. See - Atula-(1). ( Pala means  metal weight; a measure of metal)

tulādhāra.p: [Tulā+dhara+ṇa] (pu) CL=7 (1) (a) It weighs (by a weight scale). (B) (Merchant, etc.,) who takes a weight scale. See - Tulādhāraṇa. (2) Goldsmith. See - Tulādhāramuṇḍaka. (3) It was named Tulādhāra, (A) A mountain. See - Tulādhārapabbatavihāra. (B) A village.
pn:
Tulādhāra. A mountain in the village of Vihāravāpi (Mhv.xxiii.90). It was in Rohaṇa, and the vihāra on it was the residence of Mahā Paduma, the reciter of the Jātakas, from whom Iḷanāga heard the Kapijātaka (Mhv.xxxv.30).

There was also, probably, a village of the same name as the mountain, for it is mentioned (Cv.xlvi.12) as having been given by Aggabodhi IV. for the maintenance of the Padhānaghara built by him.
